objective: T-20260929-81: after tiered spread and borrow costs, do two IPO aftermarket calendar windows still pay in 2016-2026 and from 2024 -- A: long from QP-3 signal (QP = first session on or after first trading day + 26 calendar days) to QP+2/QP+5 close; B: short after R5 >= +20% (first open to 5th close) for 20/40 sessions -- measured as an event study on the T-21 IPO event table (424B4-confirmed, non-de-SPAC, first close >= $5, median first-10-session dollar volume >= $5M) with QQQ/IWM equal-weight market adjustment.
target_regime_and_horizon: Event-driven, single-digit-session (A) and 20-40-session (B) windows after each IPO; no market-regime bet. Decisive slice: entries from 2024-01-01 (IPO reopening; 424B4-confirmed non-de-SPAC events 2024 109, 2025 147, 2026 22 before the size/volume filters), pooled 2016-2026 is the second requirement for A. Validity beyond the sampled years is not assumed; a pass would be labeled a recent-window observation with the FINRA-2241 caveat.
existing_solution_comparison: Published: Bradley-Jordan-Ritter (J. Finance 2003) 1996-2000 and Ritter-Welch 2002 describe the 25-day quiet-period convention and a 4.1% five-day abnormal return; Wolf Street (2025-12-29) documents 2025 post-pop declines among the 20 largest IPOs. Why not enough: the only quantified quiet-period evidence is bubble-era, before-cost and before the rule changed (25 days to 40 days in 2002 to a 10-day minimum under FINRA 2241 from 2015-12-24); the pop-decay evidence is a hand-picked largest-20 list measured from the offer price with no borrow or costs. No 2016+ replication or cost-inclusive test of either was found. Local: reuses the T-21 event table, price hygiene and cost tiers.
remaining_evidence_gap: No analyst-initiation dates locally, so we cannot verify that initiations still cluster at day 25 in 2016-2026 (the regulatory blackout is 10 days since 2015-12-24, so day 25 is a convention); no offer price locally (R5 is first open to fifth close, a weak proxy for the pop); no borrow availability for new issues (tiered borrow is an assumption, likely optimistic for the B family); the event table carries T-21's residual non-common-stock and ticker-mismatch errors (T-21 hand check 6/20 before the name filter, concentrated in the fallback method, which this task excludes by using only 424B4-confirmed events); ADV rank is a proxy inflated by IPO-week volume; windows with a missing exit price (delistings, hygiene masks) are dropped.
negative_experiments_checked: oc research directions check ipo (2026-09-30): dir:ipo_lockup_expiration_drift (T-21, refuted: best TEST Sharpe 0.419, placebo gate failed) is a different date (180-day lockup) and is not reopened; dir:ipo_quiet_period_expiry_and_post_pop_drift is this task's own queued row. grep -ril 'quiet period' over reports/research/control, iterations, ledger finds no earlier test of the quiet-period window (one unrelated Wikipedia-pageview source file mentions the phrase). T-21 report is read for the event table, name filter and cost tiers.
cost_and_execution_assumptions: Signal at close, fill at next open (A entry = open of QP-2, exit = close of QP+k; B entry = open of session 6, exit = close of session 5+h). Tiered spread per side from ADV rank (3/6/12/25 bp for top500/500-1000/1000-1500/beyond or unranked) copied from T-21; short borrow 3%/yr for top-1500 and 25%/yr beyond, actual/360 on calendar days held; the QQQ/IWM hedge or market adjustment is a benchmark and its cost is not charged. Prices from data/features/daily_broad pass sanitize_price_matrices defaults; events whose entry or exit price is masked are dropped and counted. IPO shares may be unborrowable; B results are an upper bound of feasibility.
stop_condition: Frozen before any return is computed. A passes only if some decision-eligible A candidate (the four QP-3 windows; the QP-2 control does not count) has pooled 2016-2026 net mean CAR >= +1.0% with IPO-date clustered t >= 2.5, entries from 2024 n >= 100 with net mean >= +1.0%, and both the +10 and -10 session shifted-QP placebo net means <= half of the real pooled mean. B passes only if a decision-eligible B candidate (the two 20-session shorts) has 2024+ net mean short return after costs and borrow >= +3% with clustered t >= 2 and a mean still > 0 after removing the three largest winning trades. If neither family passes: write 'IPO aftermarket calendar windows closed', registry refuted, no ledger and no added variants. If exactly one passes, only that family goes to the runbook section 5 screen with DSR at 12 trials, K1/K2, 20 bp and K2 increment over S3 >= 0.05.

sources.claim: FINRA Regulatory Notice 15-30 (August 2015): Rule 2241 reduces the 40-day and 25-day IPO quiet periods to a minimum of 10 days after the offering for members that acted as underwriter or dealer (effective 2015-12-24). The mandatory research blackout that made day 25 a hard date in 1996-2000 no longer exists in the 2016-2026 sample; any day-25 clustering of initiations would be a convention, not a rule.

cheapest_decisive_test.action: scripts/run_h20260929_81_ipo_aftermarket.py under scripts/run_capped.sh --mem 1.5G: build the eligible event sample, compute QQQ/IWM-adjusted CAR for the 6 A windows and 4 B windows by entry year, tiered costs and borrow, IPO-date clustered t, QP shift and random-date placebos, mirror family C, leave-out of the top-3 B winners, and machine-check every frozen gate into results.json gate_checks.
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: At least one family satisfies every frozen condition in stop_condition (A: pooled net >= +1.0% and t >= 2.5, 2024+ n >= 100 and net >= +1.0%, +-10 session placebo means <= half the real mean; B: 2024+ 20-session short net >= +3% with t >= 2 and positive after dropping the 3 largest winners).
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: Neither family passes; the QP-3 to QP+k long window and the post-pop short are then closed for 2016-2026 including 2024 onward at the registered costs.
